classification.difficultyReason: Connect two independently measured flight times through equal horizontal ranges, then simplify their ratio.

content.prompt:
Points $A$ and $B$ lie on a vertical line above the origin $O$ on the ground, with $OA=kh$ and $OB=h$, where $k>1$.

A particle is projected horizontally from $A$ with speed $U$. Some time later, a second particle is projected horizontally from $B$ with speed $V$. Both land at the same point on the ground.

Show that $\dfrac{V}{U}=\sqrt{k}$.

answer.worked:
Measure each flight time from that particle's launch.

For the particle launched from $A$:
$$\begin{aligned}x_A&=Ut,\\y_A&=kh-\frac12gt^2.\end{aligned}$$
At landing, $y_A=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=kh-\frac12gt^2,\\t&=\sqrt{\frac{2kh}{g}},\\x_A&=U\sqrt{\frac{2kh}{g}}.\end{aligned}$$
For the particle launched from $B$, let its flight time be $T$. At landing:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=h-\frac12gT^2,\\T&=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}},\\x_B&=V\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}.\end{aligned}$$
The landing points are the same, so
$$\begin{aligned}U\sqrt{\frac{2kh}{g}}&=V\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}},\\\frac{V}{U}&=\frac{\sqrt{2kh/g}}{\sqrt{2h/g}},\\\frac{V}{U}&=\sqrt{k}.\end{aligned}$$
